claim: Serial focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB/SEM) enables imaging and assessment of subcellular structures on the mesoscale (10 nm to 10 µm).
source: Serial focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB/SEM) enables imaging and assessment of subcellular structures on the mesoscale (10 nm to 10 µm).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the capability of serial FIB/SEM.

claim: When applied to vitrified samples, serial FIB/SEM is a means to target specific structures in cells and tissues while maintaining constituents' hydration shells for in situ structural biology downstream.
source: When applied to vitrified samples, serial FIB/SEM is also a means to target specific structures in cells and tissues while maintaining constituents' hydration shells for in situ structural biology downstream.
evidence: This statement describes the application and advantage of serial FIB/SEM on vitrified samples.

claim: The application of serial FIB/SEM imaging of non-stained cryogenic biological samples is limited due to low contrast, curtaining, and charging artefacts.
source: However, the application of serial FIB/SEM imaging of non-stained cryogenic biological samples is limited due to low contrast, curtaining, and charging artefacts.
evidence: This statement identifies specific technical challenges limiting the application of the technique.

claim: Using an automated workflow, three-dimensional volumes of bacteria, human cells, and tissue were produced with resolution typically achieving 20–50 nm.
source: Using an automated workflow we produced three-dimensional volumes of bacteria, human cells, and tissue, and calculated estimates for their resolution, typically achieving 20–50 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results achieved in the study.

claim: Volumetric imaging using dual-beam FIB/SEM is almost exclusively applied to fixed, resin-embedded, and stained samples.
source: Volumetric imaging using a dual-beam focussed ion beam/scanning electron microscope (FIB/SEM) enables large volumes of material to be reconstructed into three-dimensional (3D) contextual maps, for cells and tissues. However, this technique is almost exclusively applied to fixed, resin-embedded, and stained samples.
evidence: This statement describes the current state of the field regarding sample preparation for FIB/SEM.

claim: There are only a few studies demonstrating application of FIB/SEM to vitrified, frozen-hydrated material.
source: There are only a few studies demonstrating application of this technique to vitrified, frozen-hydrated material (Scher et al., 2021; Schertel et al., 2013; Zhu et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution.
source: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution but requires locating regions of interest (ROIs) within the experimental specimen (known as a lamella) sufficiently thin to be transparent to transmitted electrons (<300 nm).
evidence: This statement describes the capability and requirements of cryo-ET.

claim: Cryo-ET requires lamellae sufficiently thin (<300 nm) to be transparent to transmitted electrons.
source: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution but requires locating regions of interest (ROIs) within the experimental specimen (known as a lamella) sufficiently thin to be transparent to transmitted electrons (<300 nm).
evidence: This statement specifies the technical requirement for cryo-ET sample thickness.

claim: Lamellae are most often fabricated with cryo focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopes (cryo-FIB/SEM).
source: Lamellae are most often fabricated with cryo focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopes (cryo-FIB/SEM) (Bäuerlein and Baumeister, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the standard method for lamella fabrication.

claim: The current state of the art for lamella preparation uses Ga+ ion beams.
source: The process of thinning (milling) requires a focussed ion beam; the current state of the art uses Ga+ ion beams.
evidence: This statement describes the current standard technology for FIB milling.

claim: Correlative light microscopy (cryo-CLEM) for lamella preparation commonly employs fluorescent markers prior to and during milling.
source: For lamella preparation, ensuring the ROI is contained within the lamella commonly employs correlative light microscopy (cryo-CLEM) relying on fluorescent markers (usually a tagged protein) prior to, and during milling (DeRosier, 2021; Klein et al., 2021; Mahamid et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations describing the cryo-CLEM approach.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy under cryogenic conditions suffers from poor axial resolution (>300 nm).
source: However, fluorescence microscopy under cryogenic conditions suffers from poor axial resolution (>300 nm), reducing its effectiveness as a targeting tool for lamella preparation.
evidence: This statement identifies a specific limitation of cryo-fluorescence microscopy with a quantitative value.

claim: Shuttling between machines during cryo-CLEM can introduce alignment/handling errors.
source: Moreover, the shuttling between machines can introduce alignment/handling errors.
evidence: This statement identifies a practical limitation of the cryo-CLEM workflow.

claim: There are two alternatives to cryogenic fluorescence imaging: cryo-soft-X-ray tomography and serial FIB/SEM.
source: There are two alternatives to cryogenic fluorescence imaging: cryo-soft-X-ray tomography (Kounatidis et al., 2020) and serial FIB/SEM (Schertel et al., 2013; Spehner et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies demonstrating these alternative approaches.

claim: Cryo-soft-X-ray tomography can image volumes up to 10 µm thick at 40 nm resolution or 1 µm thick at 25 nm.
source: Cryo-soft-X-ray tomography can image volumes up to 10 µm thick at 40 nm resolution or 1 µm thick at 25 nm and has been successfully combined with fluorescence microscopy (Kounatidis et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing specific performance metrics.

claim: Soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron.
source: However, soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron and the resulting X-ray-induced beam damage can adversely affect the sample, damaging higher resolution features and precluding cryo-ET experiments.
evidence: This statement identifies a practical limitation of soft X-ray tomography.

claim: X-ray-induced beam damage from soft X-ray tomography can damage higher resolution features and preclude cryo-ET experiments.
source: However, soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron and the resulting X-ray-induced beam damage can adversely affect the sample, damaging higher resolution features and precluding cryo-ET experiments.
evidence: This statement describes a specific limitation of soft X-ray tomography for downstream applications.

claim: Serial FIB/SEM is a volumetric imaging technique where a layer from the sample surface is removed by the FIB and the newly exposed surface imaged by SEM in a repeated cycle.
source: Serial FIB/SEM is a well-known volumetric imaging technique: a layer from the sample surface is removed by the FIB and the newly exposed surface imaged by SEM in a repeated cycle (hence serial).
evidence: This statement provides a technical description of the serial FIB/SEM method.

claim: Inductively coupled plasma FIB (pFIB) ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+.
source: Such pFIB ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+ (Burnett et al., 2016), thus allowing sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove the large volumes of material found in tissue samples (as opposed to single cells).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and describes a technical advantage of pFIB.

claim: Higher currents from pFIB allow sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove large volumes of material found in tissue samples.
source: Such pFIB ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+ (Burnett et al., 2016), thus allowing sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove the large volumes of material found in tissue samples (as opposed to single cells).
evidence: This statement describes the practical advantage of higher pFIB currents for tissue imaging.

claim: A potential advantage of pFIB is a reduction in ion implantation into the sample compared to Ga+ FIB.
source: A potential further advantage is a reduction in ion implantation into the sample which is known to occur when Ga+ FIB is used with solid-state chemical specimens (Eder et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and describes a potential advantage of pFIB.

claim: Imaging native contrast of biological material using serial FIB/SEM is difficult because the interaction with low atomic number elements results in fewer backscattered and secondary electrons.
source: Imaging native contrast of biological material using serial FIB/SEM is difficult. The interaction with low atomic number elements results in fewer backscattered and consequently secondary electrons (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980) and therefore images have inherently low sample contrast (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations explaining the physical basis for low contrast.

claim: Sample contrast in biological SEM imaging has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal.
source: Sample contrast has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal. However, this leads to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
evidence: This statement describes the traditional approach and its limitations.

claim: Fixation and heavy metal staining lead to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, preventing near-atomic resolution analysis of constituent proteins.
source: Sample contrast has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal. However, this leads to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
evidence: This statement describes the limitations of traditional sample preparation methods.

claim: For insulating materials like biological materials, there are two primary electron energies where the secondary electron yield equals the number of incident electrons (crossover energies).
source: For insulating materials, such as biological materials, there are two primary electron energies where the secondary electron yield is equal to the number of incident electrons – so called crossover energies.
evidence: This statement describes a physical property of electron-material interactions.

claim: Imaging at crossover energies stabilises the potential of the surface and reduces charging.
source: Imaging at these energies stabilises the potential of the surface and reduces charging (Joy and Joy, 1996; Seiler, 1983).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations describing the effect of imaging at crossover energies.

claim: Different plasma gases were evaluated for their suitability in cryo-serial pFIB/SEM of vitrified hydrated biological specimens.
source: Here, we report serial cryogenic plasma FIB/SEM (cryo-serial pFIB/SEM) analysis of vitrified hydrated biological specimens. We evaluated different plasma gases for their suitability and obtained serially generated volumes with high biological contrast.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: An automated data collection routine was described that maximises image contrast and feature localisation.
source: We describe an automated data collection routine that maximises image contrast and feature localisation.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: A range of samples from bacteria, cells, and tissue were imaged demonstrating the ability of the technique to generate subcellular information suitable for targeting.
source: Using this approach we imaged a range of samples from bacteria, cells, and tissue demonstrating the ability of the technique applied to vitrified material to generate subcellular information that may be suitable for targeting.
evidence: This statement summarizes the experimental results demonstrating the technique's capabilities.

claim: Nascent chromatophores were observed in photosynthetic bacteria.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation made in the study.

claim: In mammalian cells, the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network were quantified.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes quantitative analysis performed on mammalian cell data.

claim: In vitrified mouse brain, synapses and synaptic contents were observed.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed in brain tissue.

claim: In mouse heart, the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue were observed.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed in heart tissue.

claim: Curtaining propensity was assessed at three ion currents (high, medium, and low) for four different gases (argon, xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen) at two different voltages (30 and 20 kV).
source: We determined the curtaining propensity (expressed as % score) at three ion currents (high, medium, and low) to analyse this relationship for four different gases (argon, xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen) at two different voltages (30 and 20 kV) (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental design for evaluating curtaining, with supporting figures.

claim: Variations in curtaining showed a trend towards greater curtaining propensity at high currents vs. low currents.
source: Variations in the curtaining showed a trend towards greater curtaining propensity at high currents vs. low currents.
evidence: This statement describes an observed trend in the curtaining data.

claim: Nitrogen at 20 kV is a notable exception to the trend of greater curtaining at high currents.
source: The notable exception to this is nitrogen at 20 kV (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement identifies a specific exception to the general trend, supported by a figure.

claim: Nitrogen and oxygen plasmas exhibit the greatest proportion of curtaining artefacts compared to xenon and argon at high, medium, and low currents.
source: Nitrogen and oxygen plasmas exhibit the greatest proportion of curtaining artefacts compared to xenon and argon at high, medium, and low currents.
evidence: This statement summarizes a comparison of curtaining propensity across different gases.

claim: Plasmas generated from xenon and argon produce the smoothest surfaces for bulk milling and pFIB/SEM imaging.
source: Plasmas generated from xenon and argon produce the smoothest surfaces for bulk milling and pFIB/SEM imaging (Figure 1).
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the curtaining data, supported by a figure.

claim: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents.
source: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents while argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of curtaining propensity for argon and xenon.

claim: Argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
source: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents while argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
evidence: This statement provides a comparative assessment of argon vs. xenon at higher currents.

claim: During automated serial pFIB/SEM on cells and tissues, no trends in the accumulation of curtains or detectable changes in curtaining propensity over time were observed.
source: During automated serial pFIB/SEM on cells and tissues we did not observe any trends in the accumulation of curtains or detectable changes in curtaining propensity over time.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about the temporal stability of curtaining during data acquisition.

claim: The smallest probe size for plasma ion beams is considerably larger than that reported for Ga-based sources for the corresponding current.
source: As expected, the smallest probe size is considerably larger than the one reported for Ga-based source for the corresponding current (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Vitale and Sugar, 2022).
evidence: This statement compares plasma ion beam probe sizes to Ga+ sources, supported by a figure and citation.

claim: At 30 kV, probe sizes were smallest with argon, with xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen all being similar.
source: At 30 kV, we observed that probe sizes were smallest with argon, with xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen all being similar.
evidence: This statement describes a specific observation about probe sizes at 30 kV.

claim: At 20 kV, the spot size for the different sources used are similar with argon and xenon showing an early plateau while oxygen and nitrogen increased linearly.
source: Interestingly at 20 kV, the spot size for the different sources used are similar with argon and xenon showing an early plateau while oxygen and nitrogen increased linearly.
evidence: This statement describes a specific observation about probe size behavior at 20 kV.

claim: A milling step of 50 nm was chosen based on a compromise between workflow and electron interaction depth.
source: We used a milling step of 50 nm. This step depth was chosen based on a compromise between workflow and electron interaction depth.
evidence: This statement explains the rationale for choosing a specific milling step size.

claim: The electron interaction depth was estimated to be 30 nm for entirely biological polymers.
source: The interaction depth was informed by the work from Haase and colleagues (Guehrs et al., 2017) who estimated this to be 30 nm for entirely biological polymers and whilst imagining of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm (Seiter et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing an estimate of interaction depth.

claim: Imaging of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm.
source: The interaction depth was informed by the work from Haase and colleagues (Guehrs et al., 2017) who estimated this to be 30 nm for entirely biological polymers and whilst imagining of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm (Seiter et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing an estimate of interaction depth for a specific sample type.

claim: The best imaging parameters are between 1.1 and 1.2 kV (low kV), with a current between 6.3 and 13 pA (low current).
source: In our hands the best imaging parameters are between 1.1 and 1.2 kV (low kV), with a current between 6.3 and 13 pA (low current).
evidence: This statement describes the optimized imaging parameters determined in the study.

claim: A short dwell time (100 ns) coupled with line integration (50–100) gave optimal contrast and low charging artefact.
source: We found a short dwell time (100 ns) coupled with line integration (50–100) gave optimal contrast and low charging artefact.
evidence: This statement describes optimized imaging parameters for contrast and artifact reduction.

claim: 500 slices were recorded on plunge-frozen HeLa cells.
source: We recorded 500 slices on plunge-frozen HeLa cell and clearly visualised various membranous compartments, such as nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This statement describes the extent of data acquisition on HeLa cells.

claim: Various membranous compartments were clearly visualised in HeLa cells, including nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae.
source: We recorded 500 slices on plunge-frozen HeLa cell and clearly visualised various membranous compartments, such as nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed in the HeLa cell data, supported by figures.

claim: Two centrosomes were observed in HeLa cells, recognisable by their respective pairs of centrioles.
source: We observed two centrosomes, recognisable by their respective pairs of centrioles characterised by their archetypal barrel/wheel shape associated to a pericentriolar matrix (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This statement describes a specific observation of cellular structures in HeLa cells, supported by figures.

claim: The distance between the centre of the two centrosomes is approximately 1.2 µm, consistent with the cell in prophase.
source: The distance between the centre of the two centrosomes is approximately 1.2 µm consistent with the cell in the prophase (Figure 2E; Kaseda et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement and interpretation supported by a figure and citation.

claim: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other.
source: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other, a heterogeneity not uncommon for cells in division (Figure 2E; Vitiello et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of centriole spacing, supported by a figure and citation.

claim: The heterogeneity in centriole spacing is not uncommon for cells in division.
source: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other, a heterogeneity not uncommon for cells in division (Figure 2E; Vitiello et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing context for the observed heterogeneity.

claim: Spindle microtubules were not observed between the two centrosomes.
source: However, the spindle microtubules were not observed between the two centrosomes.
evidence: This statement describes the absence of a specific cellular structure in the data.

claim: The brain tissue imaged volume was 844.4 µm3 (20.7 × 13.8 × 3 µm3).
source: The brain tissue imaged volume was 844.4 µm3 (20.7 × 13.8 × 3 µm3) and therefore permits observation of a range of cell types including neurons and oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative information about the volume of brain tissue imaged.

claim: The brain tissue volume permits observation of a range of cell types including neurons and oligodendrocytes.
source: The brain tissue imaged volume was 844.4 µm3 (20.7 × 13.8 × 3 µm3) and therefore permits observation of a range of cell types including neurons and oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This statement describes the types of cells observable in the brain tissue volume.

claim: Cellular interactions were observed, including the envelopment of axons by oligodendrocytes.
source: Cellular interactions were observed, including the envelopment of axons by oligodendrocytes (visible as black contrast in images due to the high myelin [lipid] content).
evidence: This statement describes a specific cellular interaction observed in the brain tissue data.

claim: The diameter of myelinated neurons ranged from ~0.53 to ~2.8 µm (longest cross-section, mean 1.02±0.73 µm).
source: The diameter of these myelinated neurons ranged from ~0.53 to ~2.8 µm (longest cross-section, mean 1.02±0.73 µm) demonstrating that these can be highly variable.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of myelinated neuron diameters.

claim: Nuclei and mitochondria were clearly observed within cells in brain tissue, including the visualisation of mitochondrial cristae.
source: Within cells we clearly observed nuclei and mitochondria (approx. 87 in the acquired volume), including the visualisation of their cristae (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement describes specific cellular structures observed in brain tissue, supported by a figure.

claim: Approximately 87 mitochondria were observed in the acquired brain tissue volume.
source: Within cells we clearly observed nuclei and mitochondria (approx. 87 in the acquired volume), including the visualisation of their cristae (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative count of mitochondria in the brain tissue volume.

claim: Synaptic junctions were visible in brain tissue, and pre-synaptic vesicles (typically 20–30 nm diameter) were discerned within the pre-synaptic terminal.
source: Synaptic junctions were visible, and we were able to discern the presence of pre-synaptic vesicles (typically 20–30 nm diameter) within the pre-synaptic terminal.
evidence: This statement describes specific synaptic structures observed with size measurements.

claim: Within one synaptic terminal (Synapse I), ~184 vesicles were identified.
source: Within one terminal, ~184 vesicles were identified (Synapse I, Figure 3A–C), whereas in a second, ~98 were identified (Synapse II, Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative count of vesicles in a specific synapse, supported by figures.

claim: In a second synaptic terminal (Synapse II), ~98 vesicles were identified.
source: Within one terminal, ~184 vesicles were identified (Synapse I, Figure 3A–C), whereas in a second, ~98 were identified (Synapse II, Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative count of vesicles in a second synapse, supported by a figure.

claim: On the post-synaptic neuron, the post-synaptic density could be visualised.
source: On the post-synaptic neuron, the post-synaptic density could be visualised (Figure 3; Valtschanoff and Weinberg, 2001).
evidence: This statement describes a specific synaptic structure observed, supported by a figure and citation.

claim: The morphologies of the synapses were very diverse, sometimes with multiple pre-synaptic terminals forming on one post-synaptic face.
source: The morphologies of the synapses were very diverse, sometimes with multiple pre-synaptic terminals forming on one post-synaptic face (Figure 3A), highlighting the diversity prevalent in synaptic junctions in tissue.
evidence: This statement describes the observed diversity in synaptic morphology, supported by a figure.

claim: The diversity in synaptic morphology is consistent with previous studies.
source: Such diversity is consistent with previous studies (Santuy et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation comparing the observed diversity to prior work.

claim: Imaging 90° to the milled sample surface improves image quality compared to imaging at 52°.
source: The contrast improvement when SEM images are taken at 90° (Figure 4C–E) is immediately visible, features within images acquired at 52° are less pronounced compared to imaging at 90° to the surface, with features such as the nucleus, cytoplasmic vesicles, and bacterial inclusions, while discernible in both angles, are much more prominent in images acquired at 90°.
evidence: This statement describes a comparison of image quality at different imaging angles, supported by figures.

claim: The outer membrane of bacteria is low contrast when imaged at 52°, but prominently seen at 90°.
source: The outer membrane of the bacteria exemplifies a case where features are low contrast when imaged at 52°, but which at 90° can be prominently seen in the images (Figure 4E arrows).
evidence: This statement describes a specific example of improved contrast at 90°, supported by a figure.

claim: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm.
source: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm, while using the same assessment with SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV (Figure 4J).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative resolution measurement for 52° imaging, supported by a figure.

claim: SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV.
source: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm, while using the same assessment with SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV (Figure 4J).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative resolution measurement for 90° imaging, supported by a figure.

claim: Manual imaging at 52° with optimisation of focus improved the reported resolution.
source: Manual imaging at 52° with optimisation of focus improved the reported resolution (Figure 4G and H and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement describes an improvement in resolution with manual optimization, supported by figures.

claim: Even with manual control, 90° imaging yields more detail and higher contrast than 52° imaging due to differences in electron collection efficiency.
source: However, visual analysis of features including the outer membrane show that even with manual control, 90° imaging yields more detail and higher contrast due to differences in electron collection efficiency which is maximal when normal to the SEM (Wells, 1975).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation explaining the physical basis for improved contrast at 90°.

claim: The XY shift was measured to be 52±38 nm without stage movement, and 96±71 nm with stage movement.
source: The XY shift was calculated as the shift between features and measured to be 52±38 nm without stage movement, and 96±71 nm with stage movement.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of XY shift with and without stage movement.

claim: Stage movement results in twofold increase in drift, however the absolute magnitude of the drift is small, representing under 1% of the FOV.
source: Thus, stage movement results in twofold increase in drift, however the absolute magnitude of the drift is small, representing under 1% of the FOV (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This statement provides an interpretation of the drift measurements, supported by a figure.

claim: For a targeted milling step of 50 nm, the observed steps were 48.1±1.4 nm without stage movement and 48.9±4 nm with stage movement.
source: For a targeted milling step of 50 nm, the observed steps were 48.1±1.4 nm without stage movement and 48.9±4 nm with stage movement.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of actual milling step sizes.

claim: Z-drift is minimal and not increased by the tilting regime.
source: Z-drift is therefore minimal and not increased by the tilting regime (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C, D).
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the Z-drift measurements, supported by a figure.

claim: The targeted Z step (50 nm) is achievable under cryogenic conditions.
source: Moreover, this experiment confirms the targeted Z step (50 nm) is achievable under cryogenic conditions (Chan and Chason, 2007).
evidence: This statement is a conclusion supported by the experimental data and a citation.

claim: At both 1 and 2kV imaging energy, the depth of field was found to be ~20 µm.
source: At both 1 and 2kV imaging energy, this was found to be ~20 µm (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of depth of field, supported by a figure.

claim: Using a slice thickness of 50 nm, a focus correction will be needed after around 400 slices.
source: Using a slice thickness of 50 nm, a focus correction will be needed after around 400 slices.
evidence: This statement is a calculation based on the depth of field measurement.

claim: Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed in plunge-frozen R. rubrum imaged in a frozen-hydrated state, absent of stain or fixative.
source: Plunge-frozen R. rubrum were imaged in a frozen-hydrated state, absent of stain or fixative (Figure 5). Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed, and biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes, thought to be 30–80 nm apart (Tucker et al., 2010), were clearly distinguished within the pFIB/SEM image stack (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This statement describes the quality of the R. rubrum data, supported by figures.

claim: Biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes, thought to be 30–80 nm apart, were clearly distinguished in R. rubrum.
source: Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed, and biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes, thought to be 30–80 nm apart (Tucker et al., 2010), were clearly distinguished within the pFIB/SEM image stack (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed, with a citation for the expected membrane spacing.

claim: Collection of the R. rubrum dataset was accomplished in 2.5 hr in an automated manner.
source: Collection of the dataset was accomplished in 2.5 hr in an automated manner.
evidence: This statement provides information about the data acquisition time and automation.

claim: Both developing and mature chromatophores were observed in R. rubrum; mature chromatophores are ~30–60 nm in diameter.
source: We observed both developing and mature chromatophores; the roughly spherical vesicles which contain the photosynthetic apparatus and are ~30–60 nm in diameter when mature (Tucker et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement describes observed structures with size information supported by a citation.

claim: Nascent chromatophores budding from the inner membrane were unambiguously discerned in R. rubrum.
source: Nascent chromatophores budding from the inner membrane were unambiguously discerned (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation, supported by a figure.

claim: The formation of chromatophores had previously not been visualised on this scale.
source: The formation of these chromatophores had previously not been visualised on this scale.
evidence: This statement claims a novel observation compared to prior work.

claim: In eight segmented R. rubrum cells, 2772 mature and 84 nascent chromatophores were observed.
source: In the eight cells which we segmented, 2772 mature and 84 nascent chromatophores were observed.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative counts of chromatophores from segmented data.

claim: The segmented R. rubrum data comprises ~33% of the total number of cells, hence an estimated ~8000 chromatophores would be available for analysis in the full volume.
source: The segmented data comprises ~33% of the total number of cells, hence an estimated ~8000 chromatophores would be available for analysis in the full volume.
evidence: This statement provides an extrapolation from the segmented data to the full volume.

claim: Nascent chromatophores were unevenly distributed across the population of R. rubrum cells.
source: We noted that the nascent chromatophores were unevenly distributed across the population of cells; in one of the segmented cell, ~12% of the total chromatophores were nascent whereas the majority of cells imaged had very few or none.
evidence: This statement describes the distribution of nascent chromatophores across cells.

claim: In one R. rubrum cell, ~12% of the total chromatophores were nascent whereas the majority of cells imaged had very few or none.
source: We noted that the nascent chromatophores were unevenly distributed across the population of cells; in one of the segmented cell, ~12% of the total chromatophores were nascent whereas the majority of cells imaged had very few or none.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of nascent chromatophore abundance across cells.

claim: The ability of serial pFIB/SEM to image large volumes quickly allows rare events such as chromatophore budding to be observed.
source: The ability of serial pFIB/SEM ability to image large volumes quickly allows rare events such as chromatophore budding to be observed.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion about the advantage of the technique for observing rare events.

claim: Plunge-frozen vitrified Vero cells were milled using nitrogen.
source: Plunge-frozen vitrified Vero cells were milled using nitrogen.
evidence: This statement describes the sample preparation and milling gas used for Vero cells.

claim: Imaging Vero cells with nitrogen severely limited the software's ability to track the milling area, reflected in the number of Z slices acquired (46 slices vs. 500 for HeLa).
source: Imaging with nitrogen severely limited the software's ability to track the milling area, this is reflected in the number of Z slices acquired when compared to HeLa cells (46 slices vs. 500 for HeLa).
evidence: This statement describes a technical limitation when using nitrogen plasma, with quantitative comparison.

claim: The Vero cell volume was acquired after seven previous attempts to automate serial pFIB/SEM acquisition.
source: This volume was also acquired after seven previous attempts to automate serial pFIB/SEM acquisition.
evidence: This statement describes the difficulty in automating the acquisition with nitrogen plasma.

claim: Subcellular structure was clearly seen in Vero cells, including large protein complexes such as nuclear pore complexes (NPCs).
source: However, we were able to clearly see subcellular structure. In addition to membranous organelles, we identified large protein complexes within the cellular volumes. Nuclear pore complexes (NPCs) were observed (Figure 6A) within cells permitting us to visualise their organisation within the cell, with 138 NPCs being visible within the data.
evidence: This statement describes specific structures observed in Vero cells, supported by a figure.

claim: 138 NPCs were visible within the Vero cell data.
source: Nuclear pore complexes (NPCs) were observed (Figure 6A) within cells permitting us to visualise their organisation within the cell, with 138 NPCs being visible within the data.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative count of NPCs, supported by a figure.

claim: The mitochondrial network was characterised in Vero cells with isolated mitochondria, small mitochondrial networks, and large networks identifiable.
source: The mitochondrial network (Shen et al., 2022) was also characterised (Figure 6A, B and D) with isolated mitochondria (mitochondria 16 and 17), small mitochondrial networks (12 and 14), and large networks (2 and 7) identifiable.
evidence: This statement describes the characterization of mitochondrial networks, supported by figures and a citation.

claim: The volume taken up by mitochondria, ER and LDs within the Vero cell imaged volume was calculated.
source: We calculated the volume taken up by mitochondria, ER and LDs within the imaged volume (Figure 6D and E), and quantified the number and size of contacts of the ER with LDs or with mitochondria (Figure 6A, B and E).
evidence: This statement describes quantitative analysis performed on the Vero cell data, supported by figures.

claim: In Vero cells, 26 LD-to-ER contacts and 48 mitochondria-to-ER MCS were identified.
source: In Vero cells, we identified 26 LD-to-ER contacts and 48 mitochondria-to-ER MCS (Giacomello and Pellegrini, 2016; Jacquemyn et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement provides quantitative counts of membrane contact sites, supported by citations.

claim: Both LD-ER and mitochondria-ER MCS have a similar volume (1–5 × 10–3 µm3) and Gaussian distribution.
source: Both LD-ER and mitochondria-ER MCS have a similar volume (1–5 × 10–3 µm3) (Figure 6A) and Gaussian distribution.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative analysis of MCS volumes, supported by a figure.

claim: The similar distribution of LD-ER and mitochondria-ER MCS suggests a limit in the extent to which the ER can track and contact an organelle.
source: Interestingly, the distribution is the same, suggesting a limit in the extent of which the ER can track and contact an organelle.
evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the observed similarity in MCS distributions.

claim: Fixed (4% paraformaldehyde) heart tissue was sectioned and subsequently vitrified for cryo-serial pFIB/SEM.
source: We further demonstrated the use of normal (90°) imaging applied to fixed (4% paraformaldehyde) heart tissue, which was sectioned and subsequently vitrified in a similar manner as described for brain tissue.
evidence: This statement describes the sample preparation method for heart tissue.

claim: Fixation was used to preserve tissue integrity in the time between sectioning where the tissue may have degraded.
source: Fixation was used to preserve tissue integrity in the time between sectioning where the tissue may have degraded.
evidence: This statement explains the rationale for using fixation in the heart tissue preparation.

claim: Sarcomere-containing regions (myofibrils) were visualised in heart tissue sandwiched between columns of mitochondria.
source: Sarcomere-containing regions (myofibrils) were visualised sandwiched between columns of mitochondria, running along and at oblique angles with respect to the milling direction (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement describes specific structures observed in heart tissue, supported by a figure.

claim: The Z-disc, I-band, and A-bands of the sarcomeres were visible in heart tissue, along with a putative M-line.
source: The Z-disc, I-band, and A-bands of the sarcomeres were visible, along with a putative M-line (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This statement describes specific sarcomere structures observed, supported by figures.

claim: The average sarcomere length in heart tissue samples was 1.68 µm (SD = 0.03, N=34).
source: The average sarcomere length in these samples was 1.68 µm (SD = 0.03, N=34).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of sarcomere length.

claim: One nucleus was seen in heart tissue with associated NPCs and putative hetero/euchromatin regions.
source: As cardiomyocytes are syncytial, they have multiple nuclei. One nucleus was seen with associated NPCs and putative hetero/euchromatin regions.
evidence: This statement describes nuclear structures observed in heart tissue.

claim: Blood vessels in heart tissue were identified by the characteristic layer of endothelial cells and red blood cells (bi-lobal shape).
source: Blood vessels, in proximity to the cell, were identified by the characteristic layer of endothelial cells and red blood cells (bi-lobal shape) (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement describes how blood vessels were identified, supported by a figure.

claim: In the heart volume examined (2698.4 µm3), 997 mitochondria were visualised.
source: In the heart volume examined (2698.4 µm3), 997 mitochondria were visualised.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative information about the heart tissue volume and mitochondrial count.

claim: The relative concentration of mitochondria in heart tissue is 0.36 mitochondria/µm3 (c.f. 0.10 for mouse brain).
source: This gives a relative concentration of mitochondria of 0.36 mitochondria/µm3 for heart tissue (c.f. 0.10 for mouse brain), which agrees with previous observations of mitochondrial content in mouse heart tissues (Else and Hulbert, 1985).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of mitochondrial density between tissues, supported by a citation.

claim: The mitochondrial concentration in heart tissue agrees with previous observations of mitochondrial content in mouse heart tissues.
source: This gives a relative concentration of mitochondria of 0.36 mitochondria/µm3 for heart tissue (c.f. 0.10 for mouse brain), which agrees with previous observations of mitochondrial content in mouse heart tissues (Else and Hulbert, 1985).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation comparing the measured value to prior work.

claim: The brain section and HeLa cells, which were acquired using the same software, angle, and pixel size, present different resolutions.
source: Interestingly, the brain section and HeLa cells, which were acquired using the same software, angle, and pixel size, present different resolutions reflecting the importance of other parameters such as focussing and astigmatism, as well as sample to sample variability.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about resolution variability and its potential causes.

claim: R. rubrum and Vero cells were imaged using similar pixel size, identical software, and imaging angle, but present a difference in resolution (twofold in favour of the Vero cell).
source: R. rubrum and Vero cells were also imaged using similar pixel size, identical software, and imaging angle, but present a difference in resolution (twofold in favour of the Vero cell).
evidence: This statement describes a quantitative comparison of resolution between two samples.

claim: In each acquisition series there was no evidence for resolution degradation during data collection, even in longer data acquisition runs (HeLa cells – 500 slices).
source: We determined that in each acquisition series there was no evidence for resolution degradation during data collection, even in the case of longer data acquisition runs (HeLa cells – 500 slices).
evidence: This statement describes an observation about the stability of resolution over time during acquisition.

claim: Lamellae of R. rubrum and human retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE-1) were generated and imaged using SEM during fabrication and TEM after fabrication.
source: To validate this, we generated lamellae of R. rubrum and human retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE-1) and imaged them using SEM during fabrication and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) after fabrication.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental approach for validating compatibility with downstream cryo-ET.

claim: The final milling steps for lamella preparation generally employed lower currents (60 pA) than those used for cryo-serial pFIB/SEM imaging (200 pA).
source: The final milling steps for lamella preparation and subsequent cryo-ET analysis generally employed lower currents than those used for cryo-serial pFIB/SEM imaging (60 pA [Berger et al., 2023] vs. 200 pA).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of milling currents, supported by a citation.

claim: The SEM and TEM images of the same lamella demonstrated that it was possible to correlate features, such as subcellular structures.
source: The SEM and TEM images of the same lamella demonstrated that it was possible to correlate features, such as subcellular structures.
evidence: This statement describes the ability to correlate features between SEM and TEM imaging.

claim: Physical differences exist between the lamella imaged by SEM and that imaged by TEM when a short milling step is performed after SEM imaging.
source: Where a short milling step performed after SEM imaging there will be physical differences between the lamella imaged by SEM and that which was imaged by TEM for example, the size of the LD or compartments (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement describes expected differences between SEM and TEM images, supported by a figure.

claim: Differences between SEM and TEM images arise from the distinctive physics of the techniques; SEM images regions with approximately 25 nm depth at the surface, whereas the entire thickness of the lamella (up to 300 nm) is imaged by TEM.
source: These differences arise from the distinctive physics of the techniques; SEM images regions with approximately 25 nm depth at the surface, whereas the entire thickness of the lamella (up to 300 nm) is imaged by TEM.
evidence: This statement explains the physical basis for differences between SEM and TEM imaging.

claim: It was straightforward to correlate the photosynthetic vesicles between SEM and TEM imaging modalities.
source: Nonetheless it was straightforward to correlate the photosynthetic vesicles between the modalities.
evidence: This statement describes the ease of correlating specific features between imaging modalities.

claim: Fluorescence from chlorophyll was correlated with both pFIB/SEM and TEM images.
source: We were also able to correlate fluorescence from chlorophyll (recorded with the integral fluorescence microscope) with both pFIB/SEM and TEM images (Figure 9 and Figure 9—video 3).
evidence: This statement describes the ability to correlate fluorescence with electron microscopy images, supported by figures.

claim: Serial pFIB/SEM is suitable for correlative workflows at cryogenic temperature on near-native state samples.
source: We conclude that serial pFIB/SEM is suitable for correlative workflows at cryogenic temperature on near-native state samples.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlative imaging experiments.

claim: Charging occurs when the energetic electron beam interacts with highly insulating substances in the sample.
source: Charging occurs when the energetic electron beam interacts with highly insulating substances in the sample.
evidence: This statement explains the physical basis for charging artifacts.

claim: Charging was typically found in regions associated with greater lipid content (lipidic membranes, lipid vesicles, myelin).
source: We typically found this effect in regions associated with a greater lipid content (lipidic membranes, lipid vesicles, myelin) (Figures 2—7).
evidence: This statement describes where charging artifacts were observed, supported by figures.

claim: The presence of charging manifests as intense dark spots with asymmetric streaks along the scan direction.
source: The presence of charging manifests as intense dark spots with asymmetric streaks along the scan direction.
evidence: This statement describes the visual appearance of charging artifacts.

claim: An approach was developed that enabled computational removal of charging artefacts in images.
source: We developed an approach that enabled computational removal of charging artefacts in images.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological contribution for artifact mitigation.

claim: Comparing the automated segmentation of charge centres with the automated with manual clean-up yielded a 0.93 Dice coefficient score.
source: Comparing the automated segmentation of charge centres with the automated with manual clean-up yielded a 0.93 Dice coefficient score (Dice, 1945; Sørensen, 1948).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative assessment of the automated segmentation accuracy, supported by citations.

claim: The high Dice coefficient score (0.93) indicates that little manual clean-up was required and full automation of charge centre segmentation could be possible in future.
source: This high Dice coefficient score indicates that little manual clean-up was required and full automation of this step could be possible in future.
evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the Dice coefficient score.

claim: After charge removal the overall image resolution remains unchanged.
source: After charge removal the overall image resolution remains unchanged.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about the effect of charge mitigation on resolution.

claim: Automated segmentation of mitochondria within a cryo-serial pFIB/SEM dataset of heart tissue was performed using the neural network trained model generated in SuRVos2.
source: Here, we demonstrate the automated segmentation of mitochondria within a cryo-serial pFIB/SEM dataset of heart tissue using the neural network trained model generated in SuRVos2 and evaluate its accuracy (Figure 11).
evidence: This statement describes the application of machine learning for segmentation, supported by a figure.

claim: Automated segmentation largely agrees with manual segmentation in identifying mitochondria with a Dice score of 0.87.
source: By comparison with a manually segmented region, we could show that automated segmentation largely agrees with the manual segmentation in identifying mitochondria with a Dice score of 0.87 (Figure 11C–E).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative assessment of automated segmentation accuracy, supported by figures.

claim: The percentage of the smaller ROI segmented by SuRVos2 (24%) was largely in agreement with the percentage segmented manually (20%).
source: Additionally, the percentage of the smaller ROI segmented by SuRVos2 (24%) was largely in agreement with the percentage segmented manually (20%).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of automated vs. manual segmentation.

claim: 15 'components' were counted by SuRVos2 after the removal of segmentations with less than 1000 voxels, which is different from the total of 23 whole or part mitochondria counted in the manual segmentation.
source: Moreover, 15 'components' were counted by SuRVos2 after the removal of segmentations with less than 1000 voxels, which is different from the total of 23 whole or part mitochondria counted in the manual segmentation.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of component counts between automated and manual segmentation.

claim: Cryo-serial pFIB/SEM data can be segmented in an automated fashion.
source: Additional work would be required to better quantify the errors on counts obtained from the automated segmentation, however these results set a baseline that demonstrates cryo-serial pFIB/SEM data can be segmented in an automated fashion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the automated segmentation results.

claim: Imaging of biological materials using SEM is well known but challenging since biological material is primarily composed of light atoms (C, N, O) in a water background.
source: Imaging of biological materials using SEM is well known but challenging since biological material is primarily composed of light atoms (C, N, O) in a water background.
evidence: This statement describes a fundamental challenge in biological SEM imaging.

claim: Sample contrast in biological SEM has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal.
source: Sample contrast has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal.
evidence: This statement describes the traditional approach to improving contrast in biological SEM.

claim: Fixation and staining lead to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
source: However, this leads to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
evidence: This statement describes the limitations of traditional sample preparation for downstream analysis.

claim: The process of fixation and staining by their nature alter the underlying biological structures.
source: However, the process of fixation and staining by their nature alter the underlying biological structures (Thompson et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the effects of fixation and staining.

claim: Fixation and staining treatments are incompatible with further downstream analysis by high-resolution cryo-ET.
source: Furthermore, these treatments are incompatible with further downstream analysis by high-resolution cryo-ET.
evidence: This statement describes a limitation of traditional sample preparation for correlative workflows.

claim: All four gases tested (O, N, Ar, and Xe) can under some conditions produce smooth surfaces that are amenable to SEM imaging.
source: We evaluated different plasma gases for their suitability and obtained serially generated volumes with high biological contrast. We describe an automated data collection routine that maximises image contrast and feature localisation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gas evaluation experiments.

claim: There is a difference in the curtaining propensity depending on the used gases and ion current, with N and O showing large curtaining propensity whilst Xe and Ar showed lower propensity.
source: Our results show that there is a difference in the curtaining propensity depending on the used gases and ion current, with N and O showing large curtaining propensity whilst Xe and Ar showed lower propensity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the curtaining propensity experiments.

claim: Monatomic gases are speculated to be less reactive at the surface of biological material, and less prone to curtaining.
source: We speculate that monatomic gases are less reactive at the surface of biological material, and less prone to curtaining.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed differences in curtaining propensity.

claim: pFIB milling is effective for both plunge-frozen cells and HPF mouse tissue.
source: pFIB milling is effective for both plunge-frozen cells and HPF mouse tissue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results on different sample types.

claim: A higher tendency to produce curtain artefacts was observed in brain and heart tissue, attributed to the greater initial unevenness of the material.
source: We observed a higher tendency to produce curtain artefacts in brain and heart tissue, something we attribute to the greater initial unevenness of the material due to the presence of lumen, facias, and supportive layers which mill at different rates.
evidence: This statement describes an observation and provides an interpretation of the cause.

claim: Both composition and application method of the protective layer alter curtaining propensity.
source: Since both composition and application method of the protective layer alter curtaining propensity (Leer et al., 2009), there may be gains from further exploration of different coating approaches.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and suggests future work.

claim: The use of diatomic gasses (O, N) to generate the plasma led to double images which can be corrected for but required more manual operation.
source: The use of diatomic gasses (O, N) to generate the plasma led to double images which, as we showed, can be (to an extent) corrected for but required more manual operation (Figure 6) as there was a high failure rate of automation (>80% vs. <10% for argon).
evidence: This statement describes a technical challenge with diatomic gases, supported by a figure and quantitative comparison.

claim: The use of oxygen plasma on resin-embedded and stained samples has been reported to be effective.
source: The use of oxygen plasma on resin-embedded and stained samples has been reported to be effective (Gorelick et al., 2018) but a success rate was not reported.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation but notes a limitation in the prior work.

claim: Ar and Xe have similarly low curtaining propensity at low current; thus, both are strong candidates for exploitation in this workflow.
source: Ar and Xe have similarly low curtaining propensity at low current; thus, both are strong candidates for exploitation in this workflow.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the curtaining propensity data.

claim: At high currents Ar performed better than Xe, as demonstrated by its reduced curtaining score and visual lack of curtains.
source: At high currents Ar performed better, as demonstrated by its reduced curtaining score and visual lack of curtains.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the curtaining data at high currents.

claim: The use of pFIB to fabricate lamella has been demonstrated with plunge-frozen vitrified materials as part of a high-resolution high-throughput cryo-ET workflow.
source: The use of pFIB to fabricate lamella has been demonstrated with plunge-frozen vitrified materials as part of a high-resolution high-throughput cryo-ET workflow (Berger et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing prior work with pFIB for lamella fabrication.

claim: Milling with Ar plasma (30 kV, 60 pA) beam adversely affected the resolution of sub-tomographically averaged ribosomes within around 45 nm of the surface.
source: The cryo-ET workflow study indicated that milling with Ar plasma (30 kV, 60 pA) beam adversely affected the resolution of sub-tomographically averaged ribosomes within around 45 nm of the surface.
evidence: This statement describes a finding from a prior study about the effects of Ar plasma milling.

claim: The adverse effect on ribosome resolution was present despite the 'smooth' surface of the lamella and was attributed to damage introduced by argon ions colliding with and penetrating the sample.
source: This effect was present despite the 'smooth' surface of the lamella and was attributed to damage introduced by argon ions colliding with and penetrating the sample.
evidence: This statement describes the interpretation of the observed resolution degradation.

claim: A lack of curtaining is a necessary condition for SEM imaging, but does not necessarily indicate a lack of damage.
source: Thus, while a lack of curtaining is a necessary condition for SEM imaging, it does not necessarily indicate a lack of damage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the discussion of curtaining vs. damage.

claim: For serial pFIB/SEM, the Wattage used for argon is twofold higher than that used for the final step of lamella polishing (200 pA at 20 kV vs. 50 pA at 30 kV).
source: For serial pFIB/SEM, the Wattage used for argon is twofold higher than that used for the final step of lamella polishing (200 pA at 20 kV vs. 50 pA at 30 kV).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of milling parameters.

claim: Damage (not just curtaining) would be expected to increase with increasing current, although this has not been established.
source: Intuitively, we would expect damage (not just curtaining) to increase with increasing current, although this has not been established.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the relationship between current and damage.

claim: When comparing cryo-serial pFIB/SEM images of Vero (milled with nitrogen plasma) and HeLa (argon plasma) cells, nitrogen showed higher resolution.
source: When we compared cryo-serial pFIB/SEM (low current) images of Vero (milled with nitrogen plasma) and HeLa (argon plasma) cells, nitrogen showed higher resolution.
evidence: This statement describes a comparison of resolution between samples milled with different gases.

claim: It is possible that damage may be dependent on the plasma not simply on its current and such damage may not simply correlate with curtaining.
source: It is possible that damage may be dependent on the plasma not simply on its current and such damage may not simply correlate with curtaining, but further investigation is required.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the relationship between plasma type, damage, and curtaining.

claim: The greatest dose employed during SEM data acquisition was under 10–2 e−/Å2 over the whole scanned image.
source: SEM imaging itself will damage the sample; the greatest dose we employed during data acquisition was under 10–2 e−/Å2 over the whole scanned image, even with the smallest pixel sizes used for imaging (Table 1).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of electron dose during SEM imaging.

claim: The SEM dose used is lower than those used during cryo-ET imaging.
source: This is a lower dose than those used during cryo-ET imaging (Berger et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement provides a comparison of SEM dose to cryo-ET dose, supported by a citation.

claim: SEM-induced damage would be expected to be confined to the interaction depth, less than 50 nm.
source: SEM damage would be expected to be confined to the interaction depth, less than 50 nm, and therefore, we would expect that SEM-induced damage would be contained within the same volume (close to the surface) as the FIB damage, which is approximately 45 nm (Berger et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement provides an estimate of the depth of SEM damage, supported by a citation for FIB damage depth.

claim: Using low current, it was possible to mill in a highly controlled manner, accurately ablating a 50 nm layer reliably.
source: Using low current, we were able to mill in a highly controlled manner, accurately ablating a 50 nm layer reliably.
evidence: This statement describes the precision achieved in milling.

claim: The absolute size of the beam spot is not necessarily the limiting factor for milling resolution.
source: Importantly, the absolute size of the beam spot is not necessarily the limiting factor for milling resolution – fine control of the beam (homogeneity of beam current), careful placement of milling boxes, and a steep beam profile can enable slice thickness or final lamella thickness smaller than the beam diameter.
evidence: This statement describes factors that contribute to milling resolution beyond beam spot size.

claim: For plasma ion beams it is expected that it will be possible to ablate thinner layers.
source: Therefore, for plasma ion beams we expect it will be possible to ablate thinner layers.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future capabilities.

claim: The ideal milling step will match the depth of penetration (electron interaction) of the SEM; estimated to be between 20 and 30 nm.
source: Since SEM images are projections which lack depth information the ideal milling step will match the depth of penetration (electron interaction) of the SEM; estimated to be between 20 and 30 nm (Kanaya and Okayama, 1972).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing an estimate of electron penetration depth.

claim: The depth of penetration is a function of the elements involved and will vary by sample.
source: Moreover, the depth of penetration is a function of the elements involved and will vary by sample.
evidence: This statement describes a factor affecting electron penetration depth.

claim: 50 nm was chosen as a milling step as a compromise since smaller steps require more time and potentially introduce cumulative electron damage.
source: In this study 50 nm was chosen as a compromise since smaller steps require more time and potentially introduce cumulative electron damage.
evidence: This statement explains the rationale for the chosen milling step size.

claim: No obvious vertical discontinuities due to excessive electron dose (SEM) were noticed and features were tracked across the FOV in serial images.
source: We did not notice obvious vertical discontinuities due to excessive electron dose (SEM) and features were tracked across the FOV in serial images.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about the absence of dose-related artifacts.

claim: The rate limiting step in the automated workflow was the SEM imaging (6–7 min), with 30 s on average taken for milling.
source: The rate limiting step in the automated workflow was the SEM imaging (6–7 min), with 30 s on average taken for milling of a 20×4 µm rectangle using Ar.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative information about the time required for different steps in the workflow.

claim: Using a plasma which mills faster at low power currently would have no significant improvement in the overall time taken for cryo-serial pFIB/SEM.
source: Thus, using a plasma which mills faster at low power currently would have no significant improvement in the overall time taken for cryo-serial pFIB/SEM.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that SEM imaging is the rate-limiting step.

claim: Increasing the speed of SEM would be extremely beneficial for analyzing larger volumes.
source: However, increasing the speed of SEM would be extremely beneficial.
evidence: This is a conclusion about how to improve the overall workflow efficiency.

claim: Scanning multiple lines concomitantly and/or software solutions would enable the analysis of larger volumes and improve the integration of serial pFIB/SEM into other pipelines.
source: Scanning multiple lines concomitantly and/or software solutions (de Haan et al., 2019) would enable the analysis of larger volumes and would improve the integration of serial pFIB/SEM into other pipelines.
evidence: This statement suggests approaches for improving SEM speed, supported by a citation.

claim: The quality of the resulting cryo-serial pFIB/SEM images was excellent even with sub-optimal SEM imaging geometry.
source: The quality of the resulting cryo-serial pFIB/SEM images was excellent even with sub-optimal SEM imaging geometry.
evidence: This is a qualitative assessment of the image quality achieved.

claim: The pixel size is critical for resolution in cryo-serial pFIB/SEM images.
source: Most importantly, and not surprisingly, the pixel size is critical.
evidence: This statement identifies pixel size as a key parameter affecting resolution.

claim: Patch size was maintained at 256 x 256 for all pixel sizes in FRC analysis, which may lead to more 'optimistic' resolution estimates.
source: In our experiements, patch size was maintained at 256 x 256 for all pixel sizes, which may lead to more 'optimistic' resolution estimates.
evidence: This statement identifies a potential limitation in the resolution estimation method.

claim: The observation of macromolecular assemblies/features is consistent with the calculated resolution of better than 50 nm.
source: Nonetheless, our observation of macromolecular assemblies/features is consistent with the calculated resolution of better than 50 nm.
evidence: This statement relates the observed features to the calculated resolution.

claim: By recording 500 slices of 50 nm depth from HeLa cells, macromolecular complexes such as NPCs and centrioles were identified.
source: By imaging 500 slices of 50 nm depth from HeLa cells, we were able to identify macromolecular complexes, such as NPCs and centrioles.
evidence: This statement summarizes the biological structures identified in HeLa cells.

claim: Two centrosomes were found in HeLa cells indicating a cell in prophase but spindle microtubules were not observed.
source: We found two centrosomes indicating a cell in prophase but did not observe the spindle microtubules.
evidence: This statement describes the cell cycle stage inferred from the observed structures.

claim: In Vero cells, the mitochondrial network was delineated in exquisite detail and ER to organelle contacts were quantified.
source: In Vero cells, we delineated the mitochondrial network in exquisite detail and were even able to quantify the ER to organelle contacts.
evidence: This statement summarizes the quantitative analysis performed on Vero cells.

claim: In mouse brain tissue, complete synapses including pre-synaptic vesicles (approx. 30–50 nm) were visualised, myelin sheaths identified, and cell-cell interactions observed.
source: In mouse brain tissue, we visualised complete synapses including pre-synaptic vesicles (approx. 30–50 nm), identified myelin sheaths, and cell-cell interactions.
evidence: This statement summarizes the structures observed in brain tissue.

claim: Previous studies using SEM on high-pressure frozen cryogenic samples have demonstrated the applicability of SEM to visualise subcellular structures, including the perinuclear space.
source: Previous studies (Schertel et al., 2013) using SEM on high-pressure frozen cryogenic samples have demonstrated the applicability of SEM to visualise subcellular structures, including the perinuclear space.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing prior work.

claim: The current approach was able to identify large macromolecular complexes even within tissues, representing a significant improvement in the power of the approach.
source: Our approach was able to identify large macromolecular complexes even within tissues, representing a significant improvement in the power of the approach.
evidence: This is a conclusion comparing the current work to prior studies.

claim: Serial pFIB/SEM images could be correlated with fluorescence and TEM images showing promise for a correlated workflow.
source: Serial pFIB/SEM images could be correlated with fluorescence and TEM images showing promise for a correlated workflow.
evidence: This statement describes the demonstrated compatibility with correlative imaging.

claim: For targeting-specific ROIs within cells or tissues, SEM imaging at lower resolutions may be possible and would increase throughput of targeting ROIs on the fly.
source: For targeting-specific ROIs within cells or tissues, SEM imaging at lower resolutions may be possible and would increase throughput of targeting ROIs on the fly.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: The consequence of the highest milling currents upon the quality of TEM imaging has yet to be determined.
source: We have yet to determine the consequence of the highest milling currents upon the quality of TEM imaging.
evidence: This statement identifies an area requiring further investigation.

claim: Devitrification was not observed in the mammalian cells or bacteria imaged.
source: We did not observe devitrification in the mammalian cells or bacteria we imaged.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about sample quality.

claim: Poor vitrification was observed in the media surrounding the bacteria.
source: Poor vitrification was observed in the media surrounding the bacteria.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about vitrification quality in the surrounding medium.

claim: Comparison to non-milled samples showed that the poor vitrification resulted from sample preparation.
source: Comparison to non-milled samples showed that the poor vitrification resulted from sample preparation (David Farmer, personal communication, 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a personal communication identifying the source of poor vitrification.

claim: Sample charging was observed in all samples, most severe on lipid-rich regions.
source: In all samples, we did observe sample charging. This was most severe on lipid-rich regions.
evidence: This statement describes a consistent observation across all samples.

claim: A software mitigation approach was implemented that reduced the effect of charging on the surrounding data, though unable to recover information lost due to charging.
source: We implemented a software mitigation approach that reduced the effect of charging on the surrounding data, though this was unable to recover information that was otherwise lost due to charging.
evidence: This statement describes the capabilities and limitations of the charge mitigation approach.

claim: Preventing or reducing charging artefacts during acquisition of data would be preferable to post-processing mitigation.
source: Of course, preventing or reducing these artefacts during acquisition of data would be preferable.
evidence: This is a statement about the preferred approach to handling charging artifacts.

claim: Applying an automated, machine learning segmentation software to a serial pFIB/SEM dataset resulted in a predicted segmentation with a Dice score of 0.87.
source: Applying an automated, machine learning segmentation software to a serial pFIB/SEM data dataset resulted in a predicted segmentation with a Dice score of 0.87.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative assessment of automated segmentation accuracy.

claim: The automated segmentation was less accurate in locations where artefacts such as charging were present.
source: This segmentation was largely in agreement with the manually segmented 'ground truth' but was less accurate in locations where artefacts such as charging (Figure 11) were present.
evidence: This statement describes a limitation of the automated segmentation, supported by a figure.

claim: The enhanced contrast from imaging the sample perpendicular to the SEM paired with post-processing charge removal allowed for volumes to be segmented automatically.
source: The enhanced contrast from imaging the sample perpendicular to the SEM paired with the post-processing charge removal allowed for volumes to be segmented automatically.
evidence: This statement describes how the imaging and processing approaches enable automated segmentation.

claim: Serial pFIB/SEM can be utilised to provide quantitative information on the subcellular organisation within tissues.
source: Serial pFIB/SEM can thus be utilised to provide quantitative information on the subcellular organisation within tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the capability of the technique.

claim: A systematic comparison of Chlamydia-infected cells showed clear improvements in the definition of the ultrastructure imaging perpendicular to the surface.
source: A systematic comparison of Chlamydia-infected cells showed clear improvements in the definition of the ultrastructure imaging perpendicular to the surface.
evidence: This statement summarizes the results of the imaging angle comparison.

claim: The difference in quality between the imaging regimes was reduced but not eliminated by careful manual optimisation of the working distance.
source: The difference in quality between the imaging regimes was reduced but not eliminated by careful manual optimisation of the working distance (Figure 4).
evidence: This statement describes the effect of manual optimization on image quality, supported by a figure.

claim: Both mature and separately developing chromatophores were segmented in the photosynthetic bacteria, R. rubrum.
source: The perpendicular imaging regime does require additional movements of the stage which for a highly repetitive process can lengthen the time taken and introduce compounding errors in stage position. However, the additional time was insignificant, and we demonstrated that these additional movements have a negligible effect on the stage. We were able to segment both mature and separately developing chromatophores in the photosynthetic bacteria, R. rubrum.
evidence: This statement describes the segmentation results for R. rubrum.

claim: Unstained (but fixed) mouse heart was imaged and the Z-disc to Z-disc distance was measured as ~1.68 µm.
source: We also imaged unstained (but fixed) mouse heart. We were able to measure the Z-disc to Z-disc distance as being ~1.68 µm, which could reflect the heart being in diastole, but more likely demonstrates that the sarcomeres had undergone contraction post-mortem where typical length in vivo is ~1.7–2.3 µm (de Tombe and ter Keurs, 2016).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement from heart tissue, supported by a citation for comparison.

claim: The measured sarcomere length could reflect the heart being in diastole, but more likely demonstrates that the sarcomeres had undergone contraction post-mortem.
source: We were able to measure the Z-disc to Z-disc distance as being ~1.68 µm, which could reflect the heart being in diastole, but more likely demonstrates that the sarcomeres had undergone contraction post-mortem where typical length in vivo is ~1.7–2.3 µm (de Tombe and ter Keurs, 2016).
evidence: This statement provides an interpretation of the measured sarcomere length, supported by a citation.

claim: The images allowed accurate assessment of the mitochondrial density in heart tissue and quantitative comparison with the brain tissue.
source: The images allowed accurate assessment of the mitochondrial density in this tissue and quantitative comparison with the brain tissue.
evidence: This statement describes the quantitative analysis enabled by the imaging.

claim: The ability to visualise protein assemblies and ultrastructure in vitrified unstained tissue with laboratory-based equipment has potential applications in pathology.
source: The ability to visualise protein assemblies and ultrastructure in vitrified unstained tissue with laboratory-based equipment has potential applications in pathology, where early identification of disease mechanisms remains an unmet challenge.
evidence: This statement describes a potential application of the technique.

claim: Cryo-serial pFIB/SEM is a useful addition to the structural biology toolbox.
source: Cryo-serial pFIB/SEM is a useful addition to the structural biology toolbox.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the value of the technique.

claim: Cryo-serial pFIB/SEM can accurately determine biological ultrastructural arrangements from simple bacteria to complex tissue.
source: We have shown that it can accurately determine biological ultrastructural arrangements from simple bacteria to complex tissue.
evidence: This statement summarizes the demonstrated capabilities across different sample types.

claim: The approach can generate a 3D map of biological materials.
source: The approach can generate a 3D map of biological materials.
evidence: This statement describes a key capability of the technique.

claim: Cryo-serial pFIB/SEM is highly controllable, relatively rapid, can be done in a laboratory, and is compatible with subsequent imaging modalities.
source: The approach has several key advantages: it is highly controllable, it is relatively rapid, can be done in a laboratory, and it is compatible with subsequent imaging modalities.
evidence: This statement summarizes the key advantages of the technique.
